item.title: TypeScript types stop at the network: validating input with Zod
item.description: TypeScript makes a Node codebase much nicer to work in. But there’s one place where it quietly stops helping, and it’s exactly the place where most bugs come from: the boundary. Anything that comes from outside your process, HTTP request bodies, query strings, responses from other services, messages from a queue, environment variables, is unknown at runtime, no matter what type you put on it.
